variable_file_unreadable: The variable {variable} takes its value from the file {file}, which can't be read: {reason}.
variable_file_home: The variable {variable} takes its value from {file}, and HOME isn't set to an absolute path for its ~/.
cluster_name_invalid: The cluster name "{cluster}" isn't valid: a name has letters, digits, _, - and ., starts with a letter or a digit, and isn't workspace or user-workspace.
cluster_invalid: The cluster "{cluster}" has {key}: {value}, which isn't valid.
key_file_invalid: The key file {path} has {size} bytes, not the 32 of a key.
key_file_missing: The key file {path} isn't there, so the data keys it wrapped can't be unwrapped.
key_unwrap_failed: Run {run}'s data key can't be unwrapped with the key file {path}: it was wrapped under another key or for another run, or has been changed.
key_wrapping_unknown: Run {run}'s data key was wrapped in a way this version of Meridian doesn't know.
command_missing: Name a command, such as meridian validate workflow.yaml.
command_unknown: There is no command "{command}".{suggested, select, true { Did you mean "{suggestion}"?} other {}}
command_not_built: The command meridian {command} isn't built yet.
arguments_invalid: The arguments to meridian {command} aren't what it takes.
flag_unknown: The command meridian {command} has no option -{flag}.
flag_needs_value: The option -{flag} of meridian {command} needs a value.
flag_value_invalid: The option -{flag} of meridian {command} doesn't take "{value}".
flag_syntax: The argument "{argument}" isn't an option that meridian {command} can read.
input_path_invalid: The input path "{path}" isn't names joined with dots.
input_path_conflict: The input {path} has a value already, which isn't a group of inputs.
inputs_file_not_object: The file isn't a JSON object of input values by name.
inputs_file_extra: The file has more than one JSON value.
unexpected_error: Meridian couldn't do what it was asked: {reason}.
run_dir_exists: The run's directory {path} is there already. Meridian makes a run's directory new, so that no run shares one with another.
run_dir_not_made: Meridian couldn't make the run's directory {path}: {reason}.
socket_path_too_long: The coordinator's socket {path} is longer than the {limit} bytes a socket's path can have on this system. Set MERIDIAN_STATE_DIR to a directory with a shorter path.
socket_unusable: Meridian couldn't listen on the coordinator's socket {path}: {reason}.
socket_server_stopped: The coordinator's server on its socket {path} stopped before the run ended.
coordinator_harden_failed: Meridian can't keep your other processes out of its memory, where it holds your runs' secrets, so it won't run the workflow: {reason}.
coordinator_system_unsupported: Meridian doesn't run workflows on {os}, where it can't keep your other processes out of its memory.
run_not_found: There is no run {run} in Meridian's state directory.
source_objects_invalid: Git refused what it fetched for {location}, which isn't well formed: {reason}.
workflow_calls_itself: The workflows {chain} call each other: a workflow can't call itself, however many workflows it calls through.
workflow_nested_too_deep: The workflows {chain} call each other more than {max} levels below the run, as deep as workflows can call each other.
workflows_too_many: The run calls more than {max} {what, select, calls {times, counted on every path of calls from it} other {distinct workflows}}, as many as a run can.
workflows_too_large: The workflows the run calls hold more than {max} bytes of text in all, as much as a run's can.
child_input_missing: The workflows {chain} each call the next, and the last needs a value for its input "{input}", which the with: of the step that calls it doesn't give.
child_not_pinned: The step calls {uses}, which wasn't pinned and kept with its run's tree: the run was created by a release that didn't pin a run's whole tree.
child_dir_outside: The step's working directory puts the run it calls in {dir}, which isn't in its root run's directory.
child_not_created: The run of the workflow this step calls wasn't created: its problems follow.
owner_unmapped: Meridian can't check {path}: the owner of {dir}, on the way to it, is hidden by a user namespace, so Meridian can't tell that no other user can change it.
owner_unknown: Meridian can't tell who owns {path}, so it can't tell that no other user can change it.
directory_replaced: The directory {path} was replaced as the worker made it, so the worker doesn't use it.
path_links_too_many: The path {path} goes through more than {max} symbolic links.
database_too_new: A newer release of Meridian brought the {schema} schema of the database {path} to version {version}, and this release reads version {latest} and earlier. Use that release, or set MERIDIAN_STATE_DIR to another directory.
database_too_old: The database {path} is from an earlier release of Meridian: its {schema} schema is at version {version}, and this release reads version {latest}. A command that only shows runs doesn't change the database: use that release, or, once it no longer runs workflows here, meridian run or meridian resume of this release, which brings the database up to date.
member_settings_not_json: A member of the group "{group}" has settings that JSON can't hold, such as .nan or .inf.
worker_environment_missing: The environment meridian worker was started with doesn't set {variable}, which the backend that starts it sets.
worker_environment_invalid: The environment meridian worker was started with sets {variable} in a way it can't use.
coordinator_peer_refused: Meridian won't send the attempt's token to the coordinator's socket {path}: user {uid} serves it, not you or root.
coordinator_peer_unknown: Meridian can't tell which user serves the coordinator's socket {path}, so it won't send the attempt's token to it: {reason}.
coordinator_key_mismatch: The server at {address} doesn't hold the coordinator's key, whose hash MERIDIAN_COORDINATOR_KEY_SHA256 gives, so meridian worker won't talk to it.
coordinator_answer_invalid: The coordinator's answer to {path}, with status {status}, isn't one the worker can read{has_at, select, true {: its value at {at} isn't what the worker API defines there} other {}}.
coordinator_lost_data: The coordinator lost {data, select, events {the attempt's events from number {from}} other {a step's log from byte {from}}}, which it had stored and the worker no longer has, so the attempt can't be reported whole.
coordinator_stored_unsent: The coordinator says it stored the attempt's events up to number {seq}, past the last the worker sent, {last}.
bootstrap_token_refused: The coordinator refused the bootstrap token meridian worker was started with: the attempt it is for was claimed already, or its placement withdrawn.
bootstrap_token_in_environment: Other processes of yours can read the worker's environment on this system, so it won't take its bootstrap token from MERIDIAN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN: give it in a file, which MERIDIAN_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_FILE names.
run_plan_too_new: The run's plan is newer than this meridian reads, which is plan version {version}, so the attempt is placed again, on a worker that reads it.
attempt_superseded: The coordinator no longer takes reports from this attempt: another attempt of the job superseded it, or it ended without this worker.
attempt_lease_lapsed: Meridian stopped the job, which may run again, because it couldn't renew the attempt's lease before the lease would lapse.
worker_harden_failed: The worker can't keep your other processes out of its memory, so it won't claim the attempt: {reason}.
worker_system_unsupported: The worker doesn't run on {os}, where it can't keep your other processes out of its memory.
source_server_unknown: The GitLab server "{server}" that the step's with: $host names isn't one registered here.
compute_target_unknown: There is no compute target "{target}" in the mode {mode} here.
gitlab_server_invalid: The GitLab server "{server}" isn't a host name, with no port, such as git.example.com.
source_with_invalid: The step's with: {key} isn't {what, select, server {a GitLab server's name, a DNS name with no port, such as git.example.com} other {the path of a file in the repository, such as flows/workflow.yaml, with no empty name, . or .. in it, nor a control character}}.
input_read_as_submitted: The {type} input "{input}" was submitted as {given, select, text {text, so it's read as text} number {a number, so it's read as a number} boolean {a boolean, so it's read as a boolean} other {{given}}}.
flattened_name_taken: The inputs "{first}" and "{second}" both have their values at "{input}", as a group that flattens puts its inputs' values beside the inputs around it.
flattened_group_value: The group "{input}" flattens, so its inputs take their values by their own names: {source, select, row {the value a default row writes for "{input}"} other {the value given for "{input}"}} is kept as it is, and none of them reads it.
input_flag_unsplit: The -input number {position} has no =; write it as path=value.
input_flag_wrong_type: The -input {path} sets the input "{input}", of type {type}, which takes {type, select, boolean {true or false} number {a JSON number, such as 8, -2.5 or 1e3{reason, select, too_large {, and this is too large for one} other {}}} header {no value} other {another value}}.
input_flag_not_json: The -input {path} sets the input "{input}", of type {type}, which takes a JSON {shape, select, array {array} other {object}}, and this {reason, select, empty {is empty} extra {holds more than one JSON value} number {holds a number too large to read} other {isn't valid JSON at byte {offset}}}.
input_flag_wrong_shape: The -input {path} sets the input "{input}", of type {type}, which takes a JSON {shape, select, array {array} other {object}}, not {kind, select, string {a string} number {a number} boolean {a boolean} array {an array} object {an object} other {null}}.
input_flag_path_not_settable: The -input {path} can't set the input "{input}", which {reason, select, flattened {is of type {type}, and its inputs are set by their own names} rows {holds a list of rows; set it whole, as a JSON array} other {is of type {type}, which holds no inputs, so it has no input "{next}"}}.
fenced: Another attempt of the job has superseded this one, or the attempt has completed, so the coordinator refuses this request.
out_of_order: The report is out of order: the coordinator expects what comes next from {expected}, the number of the next event or the offset of a log's next byte.
plan_too_new: This worker doesn't read the version of the run's plan, so the coordinator sends it nothing of the run.
worker_api_too_old: This worker speaks version {version} of the worker API, and the attempt needs version {needed}, so the coordinator sends it nothing of the run.
worker_digest_mismatch: The worker that claimed the attempt runs the binary {claimed}, not {placed}, which its placement started, so the coordinator sends it nothing of the run.
fips_not_enforced: Meridian runs only with its cryptography's FIPS 140-3 mode enforced, and this process's GODEBUG has it {mode, select, on {on, but not enforced} other {off}}.
fips_module_not_validated: This meridian binary was built with the FIPS 140-3 module {version}, compiled from Go's source rather than the validated one, and Meridian runs only with the validated module.
isolation_not_built: The member "{member}" isolates its jobs {has_isolation, select, true {with "{isolation}"} other {in a container, as a member that names no isolation does}}, which its backend can't do yet. Meridian doesn't run them on the host instead, which would isolate them less.
resources_exceed_member: The job asks for {asks} {resource, select, cpu {thousandths of a CPU core} memory {bytes of memory} other {GPUs}}, more than the member "{member}" offers, {offers}.
backend_not_built: The member "{member}" runs jobs with the {backend} backend, which this release of Meridian doesn't have yet.
worker_binary_unsafe: Meridian won't start a worker from {path}, which isn't safe to run ({code}).
ssh_host_key_unknown: The {type} key that {host} presents, {fingerprint}, isn't in your known_hosts, so Meridian doesn't connect to it: it never trusts a host's key the first time it sees it.
ssh_host_key_changed: The {type} key that {host} presents, {fingerprint}, isn't the one your known_hosts has for it at {file}:{line}, so Meridian doesn't connect to it. Its key has changed, or another machine is answering for it.
ssh_host_key_revoked: The host {host} presents a key that is revoked, {fingerprint}, by your known_hosts or your SSH configuration's RevokedHostKeys, so Meridian doesn't connect to it.
ssh_algorithms_unapproved: The host {host} offers no {category, select, key-exchange {key exchange} host-key {host key type} cipher {cipher} mac {MAC} other {{category}}} that FIPS 140-3 approves and Meridian can run, so Meridian can't connect to it. It offers {offered}.
ssh_auth_failed: The host {host} refused to let {user} log in with {keys, plural, =0 {a key, since Meridian found none to offer} one {the key Meridian offered} other {any of the # keys Meridian offered}}.
ssh_config_unreadable: Meridian can't read the SSH configuration for {host} ({reason}).
ssh_config_not_read: There's no ssh client here to read your SSH configuration with, so Meridian connects to {host} with OpenSSH's defaults.
ssh_config_output_unexpected: Meridian doesn't trust what ssh -G printed for {host}: it printed {keyword} more than once, or for another host or port than Meridian asked for.
ssh_revoked_host_keys_unreadable: Meridian can't read {file}, the revoked host keys your SSH configuration names for {host} ({reason}), so it doesn't trust any key of the host's.
ssh_known_hosts_command: Your SSH configuration has a KnownHostsCommand for {host}, which Meridian doesn't run, so it doesn't connect to the host.
ssh_client_missing: There's no ssh client here to read {path}, your SSH configuration for {host}, so Meridian doesn't connect to the host.
ssh_command_unsafe: Meridian won't run {path} to connect over SSH, since it isn't safe to run ({code}).
ssh_target_unsafe: The {key} "{value}" holds a character that a shell, or ssh, could read as more than a name, so Meridian doesn't connect with it.
ssh_host_form_unsupported: The {key} "{value}" isn't a host Meridian connects to: it takes a host's name or address, or a host and its port as host:port, without a user, a URL's scheme, or another host.
ssh_known_hosts_unmatched: Meridian can't check the key of {host}: your known_hosts file {file} has hashed lines, which only ssh-keygen can match, and ssh-keygen couldn't ({reason}).
ssh_host_certificate_invalid: The host certificate that {host} presents, {fingerprint}, is signed by an authority your known_hosts names, but isn't valid ({reason}), so Meridian doesn't connect to it.
ssh_proxy_command_token: The ProxyCommand for {host} uses the token {token}, which Meridian doesn't expand, so Meridian doesn't run it.
ssh_proxy_jump_too_deep: The ProxyJumps that lead to {host} nest more than {limit} hosts deep, as ProxyJumps that lead back to themselves do, so Meridian doesn't follow them.
ssh_proxy_jump_invalid: The ProxyJump for {host} names "{hop}", which names no host, or a host or user that isn't safe to give ssh.
ssh_host_unsupported: The host {host} runs {os} on {arch}, a system Meridian's worker doesn't run on, so Meridian can't run jobs there.
ssh_worker_binary_missing: The host {host} runs {os} on {arch}, and Meridian has no binary of release {version} for that system: it looks for one at {path}.
ssh_worker_binary_unverified: The worker's binary that Meridian copied to {host} can't be kept: {found, select, none {the host has no tool to compute a file's SHA-256 digest with} other {the copy at {path} has the digest {found}, not {digest}}}.
ssh_host_missing: The member {member} of the ssh backend names no host: its remoteHost is empty, so Meridian can't run a job there.
ssh_unreachable: Meridian couldn't reach the host {host} over SSH in four tries: {reason}.
ssh_host_helper_failed: Meridian's helper on {host}, meridian host, stopped before it answered {op}: {reason}.
ssh_forwarding_refused: The sshd of {host} won't listen on {path} for Meridian's workers there, so they can't reach the coordinator.
ssh_host_release_mismatch: Meridian's helper on {host}, meridian host, is of release {release}, not {expected}, the coordinator's, so Meridian doesn't drive it.
ssh_placement_elsewhere: Meridian's connection to {host} reaches another of its nodes than the one the worker was placed on, so it can't tell whether the worker still runs.
worker_token_not_taken: The worker Meridian started didn't take its bootstrap token: {ended, select, true {it ended first, with exit status {exit}} other {it didn't ask for it within a minute, so Meridian stopped it}}. What it wrote on its standard error is in {log}.
ssh_worker_would_be_killed: Meridian won't start a worker on {host}: its system ends a user's processes as their session ends, and keeps none of yours running after your last session, so the worker would end with the session that started it. Run loginctl enable-linger there.
ssh_host_dir_unusable: Meridian can't use the directory {path} on {host}: {reason}, at {at}.
ssh_host_command_unsafe: Meridian won't run {path} on {host}, which the PATH there finds, since it isn't safe to run ({code}).
ssh_host_id_unknown: Meridian can't tell {host} from other hosts that may share its home: it has no machine ID that Meridian can read, or no name.
ssh_loginctl_missing: Meridian can't tell whether {host} would end a worker with the session that starts it: logind runs there, but the PATH there finds no loginctl to ask it.
ssh_systemd_too_old: Meridian won't start a worker on {host} in a scope of your service manager: its systemd-run is of systemd {version}, and a scope's --collect needs systemd {minimum} or later.
